script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. It's October 30th already.
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。もう10月30日ですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning, Alex. Yes, almost November.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。ええ、もうすぐ11月ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I really need my coffee. This baby schedule, you know?
script.ja: 本当にコーヒーが必要です。この赤ちゃんのスケジュール、ね？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I'm just on my second cup of tea. It's a bit drizzly out there today.
script.ja: 私は紅茶の2杯目よ。今日は外が少し小雨ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I saw the forecast. Light rain, and the low was around 11.8 degrees. High's supposed to be 23.1.
script.ja: ええ、天気予報見ました。小雨で、最低気温は11.8度くらいでしたね。最高は23.1度らしいです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It felt cool this morning. The rain probability is 37%, so maybe it won't last all day.
script.ja: 今朝は肌寒かったわ。降水確率は37%だから、一日中続くわけではないかもね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: That's a nice change from the heat, at least. But my umbrella is always wrong.
script.ja: 少なくとも暑さから解放されるのは良いですね。でも、僕の傘はいつも間違った日に持っていくんです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Did you see the news about the climbers in Nepal? Two Japanese climbers.
script.ja: ネパールでの登山者のニュース、見た？日本人登山者2人。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, that's really sad. Missing since the 15th, and they found their bodies. Terrible.
script.ja: ああ、それは本当に悲しいですね。15日から行方不明で、遺体が見つかったと。ひどい話です。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Himalayan peaks can be extremely unforgiving.
script.ja: ヒマラヤの山々は非常に厳しいものだから。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: And the other story, the Japanese journalist detained in Russia. An embassy official finally met him after nearly two weeks.
script.ja: それからもう一つ、ロシアで拘束された日本人ジャーナリストの話。2週間近く経って、やっと大使館の職員が彼と面会したとか。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, it's a difficult situation.
script.ja: ええ、困難な状況ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I feel like I read this kind of news every year. It's not going to change at my office, I can tell you that.
script.ja: 毎年こういうニュースを読んでいる気がします。僕の職場では何も変わらないでしょうね、それは断言できます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: On a slightly different note, there's a story about a Gucci 'owl fan.'
script.ja: 少し話題は変わるけど、グッチの「フクロウの扇子」という話があるわよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: An owl fan? Like, for air conditioning?
script.ja: フクロウの扇子？エアコン用のですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: No, a traditional Japanese fan, but with an owl design. And it's incredibly expensive. The article said it was 'baffling expensive.'
script.ja: 違う、伝統的な日本の扇子だけど、フクロウのデザイン。そして、信じられないくらい高価なの。記事には「baffling expensive」と書いてあったわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: 'Baffling'? What does that mean?
script.ja: 「Baffling」？それってどういう意味ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It means it's so surprising or confusing that you can't really understand it. Like, why would a fan be so expensive?
script.ja: それは、あまりにも驚きすぎて、あるいは混乱しすぎて、理解できないような状態を指すの。なぜ扇子がそんなに高いのか、みたいなね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, I see. Yeah, I buy my clothes at Uniqlo. An expensive fan is totally baffling to me. I guess I'm not in their target market.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。ええ、僕は服もユニクロで買いますから。高価な扇子は完全に baffling ですね。彼らのターゲット層じゃないんだな、きっと。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Speaking of today, October 30th... tomorrow is Halloween, right? The Daily Tanu-chan Show today is a pre-Halloween special.
script.ja: 今日、10月30日といえば…明日はハロウィーンね？今日のザ・デイリー・タヌちゃんショーは、ハロウィーン前夜祭かしら。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, yeah, The Daily Tanu-chan Show! I totally forgot to say the name earlier. My little one is too young for trick-or-treating, but my neighbor's kids are already talking about it.
script.ja: ああ、そうです、ザ・デイリー・タヌちゃんショー！さっき名前言うの、完全に忘れてました。うちの子はまだ小さすぎてトリック・オア・トリートは無理ですけど、隣の子供たちはもうその話で持ちきりです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's originally a Celtic festival, actually. And in America, kids dress up and go 'trick-or-treating,' saying "trick or treat!" to get candy. My kids still do it, even though they're teenagers.
script.ja: もともとはケルト族のお祭りなのよ。アメリカでは、子供たちが仮装して「トリック・オア・トリート！」と言いながらお菓子をもらいに近所の家を訪ねるの。うちの子たちも、ティーンエイジャーだけどまだやってるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Teenagers still go? That's kind of... cute, actually. I guess they just like the free candy.
script.ja: ティーンエイジャーでもまだ行くんですか？それって、なんか…可愛いですね。ただ無料のお菓子が欲しいだけなんでしょうけど。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Probably. It's a good excuse to hang out.
script.ja: 多分ね。友達と遊ぶ良い口実になっているのよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I'm trying to think of something fun to do with the baby for next year's Halloween. Maybe a little pumpkin costume. He's just starting to walk now, so he'll be running by then.
script.ja: 来年のハロウィーンに、赤ちゃんと何か楽しいことをしようと考えてるんです。多分、小さなカボチャのコスチュームとか。今ちょうど歩き始めたところなので、来年には走り回ってるでしょうね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That sounds nice.
script.ja: それは素敵ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Sometimes, I just want to escape for an hour, you know? Go to a sento or a sauna. Just... silence. That feeling of 'totono-u.'
script.ja: 時々、1時間だけでも逃げ出したいなって思うんですよ、ね？銭湯とかサウナとか。ただ…静かに。「ととのう」って感覚です。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yeah, that's a good idea. To just clear your head.
script.ja: ええ、それは良い考えね。頭をすっきりさせるのにね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: My wife says I'm always looking for ways to escape. I don't know why she says that.
script.ja: 妻はいつも僕が逃げ道を探してるって言うんですよ。なぜそう言うのか、僕には分かりません。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: ...You have a very energetic baby.
script.ja: …とても元気な赤ちゃんがいるからね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, he's great. Just... very energetic. All the time.
script.ja: ええ、素晴らしい子ですよ。ただ…すごく元気で。いつも。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Well, Alex, I hope you find some quiet time this weekend.
script.ja: さて、アレックス、今週末は少し静かな時間が見つかると良いわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Thanks, Sarah. You too. Enjoy your Halloween.
script.ja: ありがとうございます、サラさん。サラさんもね。ハロウィーンを楽しんでください。
